subject.title: fix: stabilize OpenClaw beta setup and PT-PT formatting

question: Should the Windows Companion default every setup to OpenClaw 2026.7.2-beta.2, retain the last setup-proven stable target, or split the lifecycle and formatting fixes from the release-target change?
rationale: Repository evidence establishes the technical tradeoff but cannot determine whether a prerelease is an acceptable supported default or how that choice should be presented to existing users.

options.title: Split and preserve stable defaults
options.body: Land the independently useful fixes while deferring the package pin until a fixed stable release passes the required WSL2 setup proof.

options.title: Approve the beta default
options.body: Explicitly accept prerelease installation as product policy after a successful fresh-install and upgrade run against 2026.7.2-beta.2 and aligned user-facing documentation.

options.title: Pause for the next stable
options.body: Hold the entire PR until OpenClaw publishes a stable build containing the lease fix and the official-package setup suites pass.

recommendation.title: Split and preserve stable defaults
recommendation.body: Land the independently useful fixes while deferring the package pin until a fixed stable release passes the required WSL2 setup proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a supported-release and upgrade-contract decision rather than a mechanical setup-code repair.
